p01.why: The body of a generic lambda is a templated context, and the lambda is never called, so the assertion is never checked.

p02.why: Dividing by zero is undefined, so the condition is not a valid constant expression.

p03.why: n is not const, so reading it is not a constant expression.

p04.why: The template is never instantiated, so its assertion is not checked.

p05.why: f is not a template, so the discarded statement is still checked, and the condition is false.

p06.why: The message must be a string literal, and msg is a variable.

p07.why: Each condition converts to true by contextual conversion, which permits a lossy conversion and an explicit conversion to bool.

p08.why: Inside its own body S is incomplete, so sizeof(S) is not valid there.

p10.why: For T = int the if constexpr branch is discarded in a template, so its assertion is not checked.

p11.why: A static assertion can be the body of an if.

p12.why: A static assertion cannot be the initializer of a for statement.

p13.why: The condition is false, and the diagnostic shows the message.

p14.why: An object is not a valid message; only string literals are.

p15.why: Both assertions hold inside a block, and main returns 0.

p16.why: 2.5 converts to true, and a lossy conversion is permitted in the condition.

p17.why: A static assertion can occur in a linkage specification.

p18.why: The assertion in the class does not need S to be complete.

p19.why: The condition is true and the message is optional.

p20.why: The template is never instantiated, so the assertion is not checked even though it does not depend on T.

p21.why: The address of a static constexpr variable is a constant, and a non-null pointer converts to true.

p23.why: A static assertion can occur at namespace scope, also in a named namespace.

p24.why: f<int> is instantiated, and sizeof(int) == 0 is false.

p25.why: sq(4) is a constant expression equal to 16.

p27.why: The message can be several adjacent string literals.

p28.why: The message can have any encoding prefix.

p29.why: The message can have any encoding prefix, including L.
